scope: Diagnostic comparison of alternate bridge transport and test-observer overhead; no application change or milestone acceptance

synthetic.method: A localhost server receives 1400 independently framed JSON messages containing the same deterministic 262144-byte pseudorandom input encoded as Base64. Both browser controls verify the combined 489385690-byte stream against independently generated SHA-256 acb3f61cd286b83d844b98c66d1ca4b1200d6eb0b9c6476fb5f0e3fc6892527f. One uses direct Playwright browser launch; the other uses launchServer/connect. They use a disposable, unauthenticated WebSocket server and do not exercise MCP.
synthetic.sdkOnly: A separate official SDK stdio echo of 1835 synthetic artifact reads, 481034240 decoded bytes, passed exact byte hashing; sampled client heaps ranged from 18221264 to 27408112 bytes and peak Job memory was 231731200 bytes. Receipt SHA-256 284c619858592a50317deda1a3cd5a1f36301d97091b07e5ed5ec7c0d000401e. This does not recreate actual browser traffic.

fullPly3.driverChange: Uses chromium.launch instead of launchServer/connect, plus the previously documented lazy assertion message. Browser cleanup is confirmed by the Windows Job guard rather than a browser-server PID in the driver ledger.
fullPly3.alternate: One experimental-transport run completed GUI Split, Extract, undo, a complete 475563378-byte public-MCP download with matching stream/file SHA-256 42b1ee32fcf658a8fadee7841eb864dfe924b9ccbdd4f6bd0598e1247358f278, GUI reopen, geometry verification and GUI undo/redo. The server recorded authentication and at least 1792 large replies on the experimental channel. Guard passed with peak 4130414592 bytes, 164552704 bytes below 4 GiB; zero owned processes remained.
fullPly3.unchangedBridge: One direct-browser run with the existing integration application completed Split, Extract, undo and full hash-matched download, but lost the browser bridge during reopen before geometry/history verification. Guard peak 4191191040 bytes was below 4 GiB, but the run failed functionally; zero owned processes remained. The screenshot shows the GUI reporting an opened project; this does not verify geometry or explain the disconnect.

limitations: The observer overhead is supported by a synthetic comparison, not a complete allocation attribution. Both full controls are single samples with different runs and time-varying memory. The alternate channel remains an insecure, incomplete prototype; no existing application contract was changed. Reproducibility, hardened security/lifecycle behavior, ownership, native, CI and milestone gates remain open.
cleanup: Guard cleanup confirmed; both downloaded project files were removed after independent hash checks or driver cleanup. Small diagnostic sources, receipts and screenshots are retained.
